 Starting 5: Emirates NBA Cup 2026 ‘Moving Day’ is here
 A look at Friday's exciting Emirates NBA Cup matchups on Moving Day, along with a recap of Thursday's action.
 NBA.com Staff
 November 20, 2026 2:25 PM NBA Nightly Recap 
 Scoot & Dame combine for 60, Spurs win 13th of last 14, Cameron Boozer has a perfect shooting night and more from Thursday.
 Another night. Another Wemby original.
 Blame a blister for the birth of “ the shunk .”
 5 STORIES IN TODAY’S EDITION 🏀 
 Cup Night 4: Stakes rise as 18 teams take the floor on Group Play “Moving Day”
 Jenkins’ Journey: How an overlooked guard became the embodiment of Detroit grit
 Surging Squads Collide: Jokić, Murray and the Nuggets welcome KD’s Rockets
 About Last Night: KAT leads Knicks in Minny, Grizz make it five, Spurs rebound, Dame boosts Blazers
 Kia MVP Ladder: Giannis soars up the rankings amid Miami’s six-game heater
 BUT FIRST … ⏰ 
 The fourth of five straight Friday ‘Cup Nights’ brings a nine-game slate, including a Prime doubleheader as the Raptors visit the Pistons ( 7:30 ET ), before the Nuggets host the Rockets ( 10 ET ).
 Anthony Edwards Update: The Wolves star continues to rehab his surgically repaired right knee, with no timetable for his return. “Whenever my knee tells me it’s ready, then I’ll be ready,” Edwards said Thursday. | Full Story 
 1. MOVING DAY: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW ENTERING NBA CUP NIGHT 4 
 Jim Poorten/NBAE via Getty Images
 In golf, “Moving Day” comes during the third round of a four-round tournament, when players look to climb the leaderboard and separate from the pack ahead of the fourth and final round.
 That’s what tonight brings in the Emirates NBA Cup, as 14 of the 18 teams in action play their third of four Group Play games.
 And with the first elimination scenarios of this year’s tournament now in play, the stakes have never been higher. | NBA Cup Hub | Elimination Scenarios 
 Staying Perfect: Orlando can improve to 3-0 tonight, while Denver and Detroit – two of just four teams yet to play two Group Play games – look to reach 2-0
 Time To Make A Move: Nine teams enter at 1-1, looking to gain ground in the standings, including two crucial 1-1 vs. 1-1 matchups
 Survival Mode: Six teams could be eliminated from Knockout Round contention tonight, including four squads – the Hornets, Pelicans, Jazz and Kings – that need a win to stay alive
 Now, let’s break it down group-by-group.
 East A: Orlando (2-0) and Detroit (1-0) look to stay unbeaten, while two others face elimination. Brooklyn is out with a loss and a Pistons win, while Milwaukee (idle) is eliminated if the Raptors and Magic both win.
 7:30 ET (Prime): Raptors (1-1) at Pistons (1-0)
 7:30 ET (League Pass): Magic (2-0) at Nets (0-1)
 East B: With Miami (2-0) leading the group, Indiana and Cleveland square off in a pivotal duel, each looking to stay in the hunt for the top spot.
 7:30 ET (League Pass): Pacers (1-1) at Cavaliers (1-1)
 East C: Another 1-1 vs. 1-1 showdown as the Wizards and Bulls battle to keep pace with Boston (2-0). Meanwhile, Charlotte needs a win to stay alive.
 7 ET (League Pass): Hornets (0-2) at Hawks (1-1)
 8 ET (League Pass): Wizards (1-1) at Bulls (1-1)
 West A: Utah needs to beat Phoenix to avoid elimination. Then – with 2-0 Dallas (idle) leading the group – Denver looks to stay unbeaten against Houston, which can shake things up with a dub.
 9:30 ET (League Pass): Suns (0-1) at Jazz (0-2)
 10 ET (Prime): Rockets (1-1) at Nuggets (1-0)
 West B: NOLA needs a win over OKC to keep its Knockout Round hopes alive, while the Thunder look to improve to 2-1 and gain ground on unbeaten Minnesota (2-0).
 8 ET (League Pass): Pelicans (0-2) at Thunder (1-1)
 West C: The night’s final matchup brings another elimination scenario, as Sacramento needs to beat the rival Lakers to stay alive.
 10 ET (League Pass): Kings (0-2) at Lakers (1-1)
 2. ON PRIME: PISTONS HOST RAPTORS + JENKINS’ JOURNEY 
 Brian Sevald + Bailey McLean/NBAE via Getty Images
 In 2024-25, Daniss Jenkins played 23 minutes all season for the Pistons.
 This year, he’s their third-leading scorer.
 Tonight on Prime (7:30 ET), Detroit looks to move to 2-0 in Group Play as it hosts Toronto. Despite battling a slew of injuries, including All-Star Jalen Duren (hamstring) missing all but two games, the Pistons sit 3rd in the East at 10-4.
 Jenkins is a big reason why. And his path to this point embodies the grit Detroit basketball is built on.
 The Long Road: A zero-star high school recruit out of Texas, Jenkins spent his first two college seasons at Pacific in California before returning to Texas for a year of JUCO ball at Odessa College. That’s when he caught the eye of a certain head coach at Iona University: Rick Pitino
 The Breakout: Known for their toughness and defensive intensity, Pitino’s teams were a natural fit for Jenkins, who followed the Hall of Fame coach from Iona to St. John’s, earning all-conference honors at both stops
 The Next Challenge: Jenkins went undrafted in 2024, signing a two-way deal with Detroit. He played just seven games for the Pistons as a rookie but made his mark with the Motor City Cruise, earning G League All-Rookie honors
 Jenkins & Pitino after a Motor City Cruise game in December 2024. (Evan Yu/NBAE via Getty Images)
 Then, another breakout. With Detroit dealing with backcourt injuries last season, Jenkins seized his opportunity, appearing in 72 games with 19 starts and averaging 9.3 ppg. By February, he’d earned a standard NBA contract.
 “Congrats to my guy [Daniss Jenkins],” wrote Pitino on X the day of the deal. “ No one is more deserving! ”
 “A lot of guys would have ran from the situation,” said Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff that February. “He works his way through whatever adversity might be in his way … and I don’t think he’s finished yet.”
 Nick Cammett/NBAE via Getty Images
 Bickerstaff was right. Now in his third season, Jenkins has become an integral piece for the Pistons, averaging 14.3 ppg while shooting 43.7% from 3.
 And he keeps getting better. After dropping a career-high 31 points on Nov. 8, Jenkins has stepped into the starting lineup for Detroit’s last five games. In those starts, he’s averaged 19 points, 5.4 assists and 1.8 steals – and the Pistons have gone 4-1.
 But it’s not the numbers that have made Jenkins indispensable. It’s everything else.
 “He’s got so many intangibles that it’s hard to keep him off the floor,” said Bickerstaff Tuesday. “Resolve. Stick-to-it-ness. Work ethic. Competitive. Selfless. Willing to do whatever it takes for the team to win …
 “Defensively, he’s dogged. He’s rugged … he takes all of it personal.”
 It’s a mentality that defines Detroit, but one Jenkins developed long before he got there.
 “It’s just my heart,” said Jenkins of his rise on Tuesday. “I always had to prove [to] everybody that I belonged … I don’t think nobody’s going to out-dog me .”
 3. PRIME NIGHTCAP: SURGING SQUADS COLLIDE IN WEST GROUP A 
 Logan Riely/NBAE via Getty Images
 Wins, victories and triumphs.
 That just about sums up life as of late for the Nuggets and Rockets.
 Tonight (10 ET, Prime),  these two streaking teams meet in West Group A, each looking to add further to their respective win columns. Houston is 1-1 in Group Play. Denver is 1-0.
 Blast Off: The Rockets are hot. They’ve won five of their last six games – a stretch that began with a 110-100 win over the Nuggets on Nov. 9
 High-Flying: Only Memphis has put forth a better attack than Houston, as the Rockets rank 2nd in offensive rating this season at 121.1
 Six different players, led by Alperen Sengun (21.6) and Kevin Durant (21.3), have averaged double-figure scoring for Ime Udoka’s crew. Sengun is questionable with an eye injury tonight, though.
 VanVleet’s Fleet: 10th-year point guard Fred VanVleet continues to run their offense, averaging 5.5 assists per game while serving as the primary playmaker
  KD Consistency: 16-time All-Star Kevin Durant has often been the recipient. For eight consecutive games, he has scored 20+ points
 “Whatever the future holds, just go in there with an open mind and get better every day,” Durant said. “I think that’s what people see when they see me on the floor in Year 20.”
 Alex Slitz/NBAE via Getty Images
 The Nuggets have triumphed in five of their last seven games – most recently, over the Celtics in a tightly contested 105-101 result Wednesday.
 Terrific Two: Jamal Murray (25.7 ppg) and Nikola Jokic (24.1) have been the team’s one-two punch thus far, and Murray leads the Association in 4th-quarter scoring (9.3 ppg)
 Flashback: When Houston and Denver last clashed, it was a night to remember for Murray. He scored 38 points – four shy of his season high – on 14-for-23 shooting
 “Just play hard on both ends, and, if you need a sub, call for it,” said the 2025-26 All-Star. “That’s my philosophy right now.”
 4. ABOUT LAST NIGHT: KNICKS & GRIZZ STAY HOT, SPURS & BLAZERS DUB
 David Sherman/NBAE via Getty Images
 The defending champs keep winning, and KAT keeps eating.
 Knicks 102, Wolves 99: Down as many as 19 in the 3rd, Minnesota used a 15-3 4th-quarter burst, capped by a LaMelo Ball triple, to pull within four and electrify the Target Center.
 But Karl-Anthony Towns answered, halting his former team’s momentum with a big bucket, before Mikal Bridges drilled a 3 to help New York regain control and hold off the Wolves. | Recap 
 KAT Love: Towns received a roaring ovation pregame from the Minnesota faithful before going to work, racking up 22 points, 12 boards, 4 dimes and 3 blocks
 KAT’s Streak: It’s his 15th double-double in as many games this season, extending his record for the longest season-opening streak in Knicks history
 The Boost, The Close: Jalen Brunson added 21 points and 7 dimes, including 14 in the 3rd, before Landry Shamet’s steal in the final seconds sealed the deal
 Here They Come: New York has now won three straight and is 9-3 in its last 12 following its 0-3 start
 Said KAT Postgame: “I was raised by Wolves, but it was Knicks in five at the end .”
 And make that five straight for the Grizz!
 Grizzlies 126, Warriors 98: Jaylen Wells couldn’t miss (22 pts, 8-10 FG, 4-5 3PM), Cam Boozer didn’t miss (16 pts, 6 reb, 5 ast, 6-6 FG), and the Grizzlies used a 71-point 2nd half to pull away from the Warriors, improving to 12-4. | Recap 
 Straight Buckets: It’s the fifth time this season Memphis has scored 125+ points while shooting at least 50% from the floor and 40% from 3 – more than any other team
 Easy Money: Memphis also went 17-for-17 from the line, marking just the fourth time a team has shot 100% on 6+ FTA this season. The Grizzlies have done it twice
 And A Bonus: It’s just the third time in franchise history Memphis has notched 12+ wins in its first 16 games
 After Detroit snapped their NBA season-best 12-game win streak on Tuesday, the Spurs bounced back Thursday.
 Spurs 124, Clippers 112: Victor Wembanyama was doing Victor Wembanyama things ( 32 pts, 11 reb, 1 shunk ), while Stephon Castle stepped up in Dylan Harper’s absence (hip strain) as San Antonio outlasted Darius Garland (23 pts, 5 ast) and the Clippers. |  Recap 
 Castle Cooks: The Year 3 guard posted 21 points, a season-high 12 dimes, 6 boards and 4 steals as six Spurs finished in double figures
 Blazers 124, Bucks 114: Damian Lillard had a day in his return to Milwaukee (33 pts, 6 reb, 5 3s) as Portland closed on an 18-6 run to take a game that featured eight ties and 20 lead changes. | Recap 
 Backcourt Boost: Scoot Henderson (27 pts, 7 reb, 5 3s) and Jrue Holiday (22 pts, 7 ast, 4 stl) combined for 49 more with Deni Avdija sidelined (foot soreness)
 5. KIA MVP LADDER FIRST LOOK: GIANNIS SOARS TO NO. 3 
 Carmen Mandato/NBAE via Getty Images
 Four days ago, he was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week (Nov. 9–Nov. 15). Two nights ago, he put on a show against his former team. And now, Giannis Antetokounmpo is racing up Shaun Powell’s Kia MVP Ladder.
 In his latest Ladder – which drops later today on NBA.com and the NBA App – Powell has Giannis jumping eight spots from No. 11 to No. 3, with his all-around dominance fueling the Heat’s six-game win streak.
 3. Giannis Antetokounmpo (MIA): “This looks like the Giannis who terrorized the opposition while with the Bucks … It’s no coincidence that Miami, after a slow start, has turned its season around as well …
 “And speaking of the Bucks, he’s fresh off a performance against his old team where he came one assist shy of a 27-point triple-double and denied a Brayden Burries dunk attempt with a filthy two-handed swat.”
 Read Powell’s full Kia MVP Ladder later today on NBA.com and the NBA App.
